topic: Physical health assessment on psychiatric admission

audits.title: An audit to assess physical health monitoring of patients following their admission to the general adult psychiatric inpatient wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust
audits.standard: Trust policy: physical health monitoring within 24 hours of admission
audits.setting: Eight general adult inpatient wards, Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Within 24 hours: BMI 91%, blood pressure 62%, serum cholesterol 59%, HbA1c 58%; QRISK calculated in 78%.

audits.intervention: not reported

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: 97% of smokers offered nicotine replacement but only 13% accepted; a 24-hour physical health checklist was proposed.
audits.citation: Hyland D, Milner A, Carter E. An audit to assess physical health monitoring of patients following their admission to the general adult psychiatric inpatient wards in Mersey Care NHS Foundation Trust. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S84-S84.

audits.title: Implementation of physical examination pro forma – a complete audit cycle
audits.standard: Mental Health Commission Judgment Support Framework version 5; target 100% physical examination on admission
audits.setting: Inner-city psychiatric ward, Phoenix Care Centre

cycle1.result: 3/13 had physical examination on admission (23%); 6 had examination in ED.

audits.intervention: Colour-coded physical examination proforma developed and implemented, with MDT and NCHD briefing.

cycle2.result: 100%: 7 examined on admission, 2 refusals documented.

audits.other_findings: Proforma to be audited every 6 months.
audits.citation: Singh Sidhu D, Molyneux G. Implementation of physical examination pro forma – a complete audit cycle. BJPsych Open. 2021;7(Suppl 1):S104-S104.

audits.standard: Lester UK Adaptation: Positive Cardiometabolic Health Resource screening and action for red-zone risk factors
audits.setting: All-male acute psychiatric ward, Livewell Southwest, Plymouth

cycle1.result: 50/63 had a Rethink template; of 41 smokers 15 not offered cessation support; 28 of 31 with BMI over 25 had no documented support; 8 of 12 hypertensive had no further action; 27 of 32 with dyslipidaemia had no intervention; 25 had no bloods

audits.intervention: Changes to admission physical health assessments, well-man clinics and improved inpatient-community communication on discharge

cycle2.result: not reported

audits.other_findings: 9 patients had no smoking status and 15 had no blood glucose test. Re-audit pending.

audits.setting: Norbury House psychiatric intensive care unit, St George's Hospital, Stafford

cycle1.result: TFTs 71%, glucose 6%, prolactin 77%, calcium 94%; unnecessary tests requested in 88% of patients (23 tests in total)

audits.title: Completing the Cycle: Re-Audit of Rotherham Specific Inpatient Physical Health Management and Documentation Following a 2021 Trust-Wide Audit
audits.standard: Trust standards: initial medical examination within 24 hours of admission, chaperone documented for examination beyond appearance/pulse/BP, patient offered choice of chaperone sex, capacity to consent documented
audits.setting: Rotherham inpatient mental health wards (acute adult, rehabilitation, PICU, older adult), RDaSH NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Trust-wide audit showed good results for examination within 24 hours and capacity consideration, but inadequate results for chaperone presence and chaperone sex preference.

audits.intervention: Recommendations from the Trust-wide audit; planned teaching at junior doctor induction

cycle2.result: Nearly 90% examined by a doctor within 24 hours; chaperone documented in only 14% of fuller examinations; no patient offered choice of chaperone gender; capacity documented in one third.

audits.other_findings: Dip sample of five patients per ward across six wards; older adult wards performed better. A further re-audit is planned after induction teaching.
audits.citation: Bell L, Jenkinson J, Allan L. Completing the Cycle: Re-Audit of Rotherham Specific Inpatient Physical Health Management and Documentation Following a 2021 Trust-Wide Audit. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S150-S150.

audits.title: Audit and Re-Audit: Improving Standardised Admission Blood Tests Adherence for Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) Patients
audits.standard: Royal College of Psychiatrists Standards for Inpatient Mental Health Services: standardised admission blood tests within 24 hours of admission
audits.setting: Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit, Kent and Medway NHS and Social Care Partnership Trust

cycle1.result: 30% had bloods within 24 hours; 40% declined or unsafe; 20% not done in timeframe; 69% of direct admissions had all relevant bloods

audits.intervention: Standardised PICU guideline with a pre-filled blood test request form

cycle2.result: Only 6% not done within timeframe; all consenting direct admissions (89%) had all standardised bloods; bloods within 24 hours increased from 80% to 94%; direct admissions with all bloods 77% to 100%

audits.other_findings: Figures remained lower for patients transferred from other wards; pre-filled forms to be rolled out trust-wide.
audits.citation: Lawson J, Zabrzycki D, Satisha S. Audit and Re-Audit: Improving Standardised Admission Blood Tests Adherence for Psychiatric Intensive Care Unit (PICU) Patients. BJPsych Open. 2023;9(Suppl 1):S166-S167.

audits.title: Improving Physical Health Monitoring on a Working-Age General Adult Inpatient Ward: A Quality Improvement Project
audits.standard: Completion and timeliness of physical health checks (examination, observations, height/weight, ECG, bloods, cardiometabolic checklist)
audits.setting: Working-age general adult acute psychiatric inpatient ward

cycle1.result: Physical examinations completed in 93%.

audits.intervention: Daily MDT reviews, job list integration and master list; then a whiteboard with colour coding for task tracking, post-MDT reviews, staff reminders and induction sessions.

cycle2.result: Physical examinations 100%; physical observations maintained at 100%; reduced delays and more BMI measurements completed.

audits.other_findings: Barriers included gender-based refusal of ECGs and reluctance of patients with eating disorders to have BMI measured.
audits.citation: Muhammed M, Jawed A, Yoganathan N. Improving Physical Health Monitoring on a Working-Age General Adult Inpatient Ward: A Quality Improvement Project. BJPsych Open. 2025;11(S1):S152-S152. doi:10.1192/bjo.2025.10408.

audits.title: Improving Admission Clerking and Physical Health Checks in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients. A Quality Improvement Project (QIP)
audits.standard: Local and trust admission protocol: clerking, mental state examination, physical examination, ECG and routine bloods all completed within 72 hours of admission
audits.setting: Battersea Bridge House Hospital, 22-bed acute mental health facility with three wards

cycle1.result: 27 patients (62.8%) completed all five criteria within 72 hours; 14 (33.6%) delayed; 2 (4.7%) refused blood tests

audits.intervention: Active physical health handover to the physical health nurse and junior doctors, with ECG available on the ward (details limited)

cycle2.result: Overall compliance for physical health checks increased from 62.4% to 96.6% after intervention

audits.other_findings: Delays were mainly due to agitation, refusal of bloods or ECG and delayed consent; reasons were not documented for 2 patients. Laboratory result delays were also noted.
audits.citation: Mubashir R, Arooj B. Improving Admission Clerking and Physical Health Checks in Acute Psychiatric Inpatients. A Quality Improvement Project (QIP). BJPsych Open. ;12(Suppl 1):S137-S137.

audits.title: Auditing improvements to physical health in the acute psychiatric inpatient setting
audits.standard: Completion of electronic physical health form within 24 and 72 hours of admission
audits.setting: Acute psychiatric inpatient ward (Kingfisher Court, Watford)

cycle1.result: Form completion 88%; 24-hour completion 47% and 72-hour completion 55%.

audits.intervention: Ward handover sheet columns added showing outstanding parts of physical clerking; later a physical health huddle in the MDT.

audits.other_findings: 266 admissions analysed in total across both periods; a biweekly physical health clinic was recommended.

audits.title: Improving physical health form completion on a general inpatient adult ward
audits.standard: Five Year Forward View for Mental Health; target ≥95% physical health form completion (HbA1c and cholesterol or declined) within 4 months
audits.setting: General adult inpatient psychiatric ward, Central and North West London NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: 61.54% of physical health forms completed (HbA1c 61.54%, cholesterol 76.92%).

audits.intervention: PDSA cycles of completion trackers: paper list, Word table, Excel spreadsheet, then colour-coded conditionally formatted Excel spreadsheet.

cycle2.result: 97.7% completion (after 100% in November, n = 34, and December, n = 39).

audits.title: Service innovation: a comparison of two approaches for physical screening of psychiatric inpatients.
audits.standard: not reported
audits.setting: Two psychiatric inpatient wards, Exeter

cycle1.result: Screening performed inconsistently and infrequently.

audits.intervention: One ward modified the admission proforma; the other set up a discharge screening clinic.

cycle2.result: Modified admission proforma raised screening rates by 4.7% on average versus 30.7% for the discharge screening clinic.

audits.other_findings: The discharge clinic gave statistically significant improvement and delivered health promotion advice.
audits.citation: Harrison MR, McMillan CF, Dickinson T. Service innovation: a comparison of two approaches for physical screening of psychiatric inpatients. Int J Psychiatry Clin Pract. 2012;16(2):157-160. doi:10.3109/13651501.2011.620128. PMID: 22122654.

audits.title: A brief intervention to improve rates and quality of physical examinations for admissions to acute adult psychiatry units.
audits.standard: Physical examination within 24 h of admission; quality scored out of 15
audits.setting: Acute adult psychiatry unit, Nepean Hospital, Sydney

cycle1.result: Physical examination in 36/71 (50.7%); mean quality score 7.5/15.

audits.intervention: Four brief peer-led feedback sessions and email correspondence to clinicians.

cycle2.result: Physical examination in 41/64 (64.1%); mean quality score 9.3/15.

audits.other_findings: Greatest gains in documentation of additional cardiac sounds (33.9% increase), additional breath sounds (17.7%), breath sounds (17.1%), cardiac sounds (14.2%) and bowel sounds (12.5%).

audits.title: Improving physical healthcare provided to psychiatric inpatients at an acute mental health trust.
audits.standard: Trust policy 'Physical Examination of Service Users during Admission to Hospital'; target 100%
audits.setting: Acute mental health inpatient unit, Coventry and Warwickshire Partnership NHS Trust

cycle1.result: One in four patients had no physical health checks

audits.intervention: Simplified paper documentation, then combined with the history taking proforma (PDSA cycles)

cycle2.result: Compliance 90%, maintained at 90% at 1 month post implementation

audits.other_findings: First cycle (simplified documentation) gave only 5% improvement; 100% target judged unrealistic due to cultural issues.
